description: Protocol-independent wire-format model instantiated for MQTT 3.1.1. The model supports reusable wire data types, multiple protocol data units, binary/text/mixed encodings, alternative framing rules, ordered layouts, and message types selected by field value, syntax, context, or transport.

data_types.name: Two Byte Integer
data_types.definition: The most significant byte precedes the least significant byte on the network.
constraints: The encoded value occupies exactly two bytes.

source.excerpt: Integer data values are 16 bits in big-endian order: the high order byte precedes the lower order byte. This means that a 16-bit word is presented on the network as Most Significant Byte (MSB), followed by Least Significant Byte (LSB).

data_types.name: UTF-8 Encoded String
data_types.representation: two-byte big-endian byte length followed by UTF-8 encoded character data
data_types.definition: The two-byte prefix gives the number of bytes in the UTF-8 encoded character data that follows.
constraints: The encoded character data length is between 0 and 65535 bytes unless a field-specific rule states otherwise.
Character data MUST be well-formed UTF-8.
Character data MUST NOT contain U+0000.

source.excerpt:
Each of these strings is prefixed with a two byte length field that gives the number of bytes in a UTF-8 encoded string itself, as illustrated in Figure 1.1 Structure of UTF-8 encoded strings below. Consequently there is a limit on the size of a string that can be passed in one of these UTF-8 encoded string components; you cannot use a string that would encode to more than 65535 bytes. Unless stated otherwise all UTF-8 encoded strings can have any length in the range 0 to 65535 bytes.

The character data in a UTF-8 encoded string MUST be well-formed UTF-8 as defined by the Unicode specification [Unicode] and restated in RFC 3629 [RFC3629]. In particular this data MUST NOT include encodings of code points between U+D800 and U+DFFF. If a Server or Client receives a Control Packet containing ill-formed UTF-8 it MUST close the Network Connection [MQTT-1.5.3-1].

A UTF-8 encoded string MUST NOT include an encoding of the null character U+0000. If a receiver (Server or Client) receives a Control Packet containing U+0000 it MUST close the Network Connection [MQTT-1.5.3-2].

data_types.name: Binary Data
data_types.representation: two-byte big-endian byte length followed by that many data bytes
data_types.definition: The two-byte prefix gives the number of binary data bytes that follow and is not included in the length.
constraints: The binary data length is between 0 and 65535 bytes.

source.excerpt:
If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.

If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).

protocol_data_units.name: MQTT Control Packet
protocol_data_units.definition: The MQTT protocol data unit, consisting of up to three ordered components: fixed header, variable header, and payload.

encoding.definition: The common packet envelope is defined in bytes and bit fields; individual variable headers and payloads use the encodings defined by their packet types.

source.section: 2.1 Structure of an MQTT Control Packet through 2.3 Variable header
source.locator: page 16 lines 223-237; page 17 lines 242-246; page 18 lines 254-265; page 19 lines 312-315
source.excerpt:
An MQTT Control Packet consists of up to three parts, always in the following order as illustrated in Figure 2.1 - Structure of an MQTT Control Packet.

Fixed header, present in all MQTT Control Packets
Variable header, present in some MQTT Control Packets
Payload, present in some MQTT Control Packets

Each MQTT Control Packet contains a fixed header.

Position: byte 1, bits 7-4. Represented as a 4-bit unsigned value, the values are listed in Table 2.1 - Control packet types.

The remaining bits [3-0] of byte 1 in the fixed header contain flags specific to each MQTT Control Packet type as listed in the Table 2.2 - Flag Bits below.

Position: starts at byte 2.

The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length.

Some types of MQTT Control Packets contain a variable header component. It resides between the fixed header and the payload. The content of the variable header varies depending on the Packet type.

framing.definition: The packet boundary is determined from the fixed header and Remaining Length, whose value counts the bytes in the variable header and payload.

source.excerpt: Position: starts at byte 2. The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length. The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.

layout.name: Fixed header
layout.definition: Present in every MQTT Control Packet and contains the Control Packet type, packet-type-specific flags, and Remaining Length.

fields.name: MQTT Control Packet type
fields.location: byte 1, bits 7-4
fields.definition: Selects the MQTT Control Packet type using the values in Table 2.1.
constraints: Values 0 and 15 are reserved and forbidden.

fields.name: Flags
fields.location: byte 1, bits 3-0
fields.definition: Uses either the fixed reserved value or PUBLISH-specific subfields defined for the selected packet type in Table 2.2.

fields.name: Remaining Length
fields.location: starts at byte 2
fields.representation: 1-4 byte variable-length integer; seven data bits and one continuation bit per byte
fields.definition: Gives the number of bytes in the variable header and payload, excluding the bytes used to encode Remaining Length.
constraints: The field contains at most four bytes.
The maximum representable value is 268435455.
A continuation bit on the fourth byte makes the packet malformed.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: Present in some MQTT Control Packet types between the fixed header and payload; its fields are defined by the selected message type.

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: Present in some MQTT Control Packet types as the third component in the defined packet order; its fields are defined by the selected message type.

type_selectors.name: MQTT Control Packet type
type_selectors.definition: The value in byte 1 bits 7-4 selects an MQTT Control Packet type and therefore the direction, flags interpretation, variable header, and payload format.

source.section: 2.2.1 MQTT Control Packet type and 2.2.2 Flags
source.locator: page 16 lines 235-239; page 17 lines 239-248; page 18 table 2.2 continuation
source.excerpt:
Position: byte 1, bits 7-4. Represented as a 4-bit unsigned value, the values are listed in Table 2.1 - Control packet types.

Table 2.1 - Control packet types:
Reserved 0 Forbidden Reserved
CONNECT 1 Client to Server Client request to connect to Server
CONNACK 2 Server to Client Connect acknowledgment
PUBLISH 3 Client to Server or Server to Client Publish message
PUBACK 4 Client to Server or Server to Client Publish acknowledgment
PUBREC 5 Client to Server or Server to Client Publish received (assured delivery part 1)
PUBREL 6 Client to Server or Server to Client Publish release (assured delivery part 2)
PUBCOMP 7 Client to Server or Server to Client Publish complete (assured delivery part 3)
SUBSCRIBE 8 Client to Server Client subscribe request
SUBACK 9 Server to Client Subscribe acknowledgment
UNSUBSCRIBE 10 Client to Server Unsubscribe request
UNSUBACK 11 Server to Client Unsubscribe acknowledgment
PINGREQ 12 Client to Server PING request
PINGRESP 13 Server to Client PING response
DISCONNECT 14 Client to Server Client is disconnecting
Reserved 15 Forbidden Reserved

The remaining bits [3-0] of byte 1 in the fixed header contain flags specific to each MQTT Control Packet type as listed in the Table 2.2 - Flag Bits below.

Table 2.2 - Flag Bits:
CONNECT Reserved 0 0 0 0
CONNACK Reserved 0 0 0 0
PUBLISH Used in MQTT 3.1.1 DUP QoS QoS RETAIN
PUBACK Reserved 0 0 0 0
PUBREC Reserved 0 0 0 0
PUBREL Reserved 0 0 1 0
PUBCOMP Reserved 0 0 0 0
SUBSCRIBE Reserved 0 0 1 0
SUBACK Reserved 0 0 0 0
UNSUBSCRIBE Reserved 0 0 1 0
UNSUBACK Reserved 0 0 0 0
PINGREQ Reserved 0 0 0 0
PINGRESP Reserved 0 0 0 0
DISCONNECT Reserved 0 0 0 0

types.name: Reserved
types.definition: Reserved Control Packet type value; use is forbidden.

types.name: CONNECT
types.definition: Client request to connect to Server.

field_overrides.definition: All CONNECT fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The CONNECT variable header contains Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive in that order.

fields.name: Protocol Name
fields.location: first field in the CONNECT variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the protocol as MQTT.
constraints: For MQTT 3.1.1 the value is exactly "MQTT", encoded as 0x00 0x04 0x4D 0x51 0x54 0x54.

source.excerpt:
The variable header for the CONNECT Packet consists of four fields in the following order: Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive.

The Protocol Name is a UTF-8 encoded string that represents the protocol name “MQTT”, capitalized as shown.

fields.name: Protocol Level
fields.location: after Protocol Name
fields.definition: Identifies the MQTT protocol revision used by the Client.
constraints: The MQTT 3.1.1 Protocol Level is 4 (0x04).

source.excerpt: The 8 bit unsigned value that represents the revision level of the protocol used by the Client. The value of the Protocol Level field for the version 3.1.1 of the protocol is 4 (0x04).

fields.name: Connect Flags
fields.location: after Protocol Level
fields.definition: Controls Session handling and the presence and interpretation of conditional CONNECT payload fields.
constraints: Bit 0 is reserved and MUST be zero.
If Will Flag is zero, Will QoS and Will Retain MUST be zero.
Will QoS MUST NOT be 3.
If User Name Flag is zero, Password Flag MUST be zero.

source.excerpt:
The Connect Flags byte contains a number of parameters specifying the behavior of the MQTT connection. It also indicates the presence or absence of fields in the payload.

Bit 7 User Name Flag; bit 6 Password Flag; bit 5 Will Retain; bits 4-3 Will QoS; bit 2 Will Flag; bit 1 Clean Session; bit 0 Reserved.

If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero. If the Will Flag is set to 1, the value of Will QoS can be 0, 1, or 2. It MUST NOT be 3. If the User Name Flag is set to 0, the Password Flag MUST be set to 0.

members.name: User Name Flag
members.definition: Indicates whether User Name is present in the payload.
constraints: The value is 0 or 1.

members.name: Password Flag
members.definition: Indicates whether Password is present in the payload.
constraints: The value is 0 or 1.
The value MUST be zero when User Name Flag is zero.

members.name: Will Retain
members.definition: Selects retained or non-retained publication of the Will Message.
constraints: The value is 0 or 1.
The value MUST be zero when Will Flag is zero.

members.name: Will QoS
members.definition: Specifies the QoS used when the Will Message is published.
constraints: The value MUST be 0, 1, or 2.
The value MUST be zero when Will Flag is zero.

members.name: Will Flag
members.definition: Indicates whether Will Topic and Will Message are present in the payload.
constraints: The value is 0 or 1.

members.name: Clean Session
members.definition: Controls the lifetime and reuse of Session state.
constraints: The value is 0 or 1.

members.name: Reserved
constraints: The value MUST be zero.

fields.name: Keep Alive
fields.location: after Connect Flags
fields.representation: MQTT Two Byte Integer measured in seconds
fields.definition: Gives the maximum permitted interval between Control Packets sent by the Client; zero disables Keep Alive inactivity disconnection.
constraints: The value is between 0 and 65535 seconds.

source.excerpt: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. A Keep Alive value of zero (0) has the effect of turning off the keep alive mechanism.

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: The CONNECT payload contains Client Identifier followed conditionally by Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, and Password in that order.

fields.name: Client Identifier
fields.location: first field in the CONNECT payload
fields.definition: Identifies the Client and the MQTT Session state associated with it.
constraints: The Server MUST allow ClientIds between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes that contain only 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ.

source.excerpt:
The Client Identifier (ClientId) identifies the Client to the Server. Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId. The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server [MQTT-3.1.3-2].

The Client Identifier (ClientId) MUST be present and MUST be the first field in the CONNECT packet payload [MQTT-3.1.3-3].

The ClientId MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-4].

The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters “0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ” [MQTT-3.1.3-5].

fields.name: Will Topic
fields.location: after Client Identifier; present exactly when Will Flag is 1
fields.definition: Identifies the Topic Name to which the Will Message is published.
constraints: The field MUST be present when Will Flag is 1 and MUST NOT be present when Will Flag is 0.

source.excerpt: These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password. If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will Topic is the next field in the payload. The Will Topic MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string.

fields.name: Will Message
fields.location: after Will Topic; present exactly when Will Flag is 1
fields.definition: Contains the Application Message to publish to the Will Topic.
constraints: The field MUST be present when Will Flag is 1 and MUST NOT be present when Will Flag is 0.

source.excerpt: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.

fields.name: User Name
fields.location: after Will Message when present; present exactly when User Name Flag is 1
fields.definition: Carries the user name supplied for authentication or authorization.
constraints: The field MUST be present when User Name Flag is 1 and MUST NOT be present when User Name Flag is 0.

source.excerpt: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The User Name MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3.

fields.name: Password
fields.location: after User Name when present; present exactly when Password Flag is 1
fields.definition: Carries the binary password supplied by the Client.
constraints: The field MUST be present when Password Flag is 1 and MUST NOT be present when Password Flag is 0.

source.excerpt: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data.

types.name: CONNACK
types.definition: Connect acknowledgment with a two-byte variable header and no payload.

field_overrides.definition: All CONNACK fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.

source.excerpt: Remaining Length field: This is the length of the variable header. For the CONNACK Packet this has the value 2.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The CONNACK variable header contains Connect Acknowledge Flags followed by Connect Return Code.

fields.name: Connect Acknowledge Flags
fields.location: first byte of the CONNACK variable header
fields.representation: one-byte bit field; bits 7-1 reserved, bit 0 Session Present
fields.definition: Carries the Session Present flag.
constraints: Bits 7-1 MUST be zero.
Bit 0 is Session Present and MUST be 0 or 1.
Session Present MUST be zero when Connect Return Code is non-zero.

source.section: 3.2.2.1 Connect Acknowledge Flags and 3.2.2.2 Session Present
source.excerpt: Byte 1 is the "Connect Acknowledge Flags". Bits 7-1 are reserved and MUST be set to 0. Bit 0 (SP) is the Session Present Flag. If a server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero return code it MUST set Session Present to 0.

fields.name: Connect Return Code
fields.location: second byte of the CONNACK variable header
fields.definition: Reports whether the connection was accepted or why it was refused.
constraints: 0x00 means Connection Accepted.
0x01 means Connection Refused, unacceptable protocol version.
0x02 means Connection Refused, identifier rejected.
0x03 means Connection Refused, Server unavailable.
0x04 means Connection Refused, bad user name or password.
0x05 means Connection Refused, not authorized.
Values 0x06 through 0xFF are reserved and MUST NOT be used.

source.excerpt: Byte 2 in the Variable header. The values for the one byte unsigned Connect Return code field are: 0x00 Connection Accepted; 0x01 unacceptable protocol version; 0x02 identifier rejected; 0x03 Server unavailable; 0x04 bad user name or password; 0x05 not authorized. Values 6-255 are reserved for future use.

field_overrides.representation: bit 3 DUP; bits 2-1 QoS; bit 0 RETAIN
field_overrides.definition: PUBLISH assigns packet-specific meanings to all four fixed-header flag bits; QoS bit value 3 is reserved and MUST NOT be used.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The PUBLISH variable header contains Topic Name followed by Packet Identifier when the Packet Identifier is present.

fields.name: Topic Name
fields.location: first field in the PUBLISH variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the information channel to which payload data is published.
constraints: The Topic Name MUST NOT contain wildcard characters.
The Topic Name MUST be at least one character long.

source.excerpt:
The variable header contains the following fields in the order: Topic Name, Packet Identifier.

The Topic Name identifies the information channel to which payload data is published.

The Topic Name MUST be present as the first field in the PUBLISH Packet Variable header. It MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string [MQTT-3.3.2-1] as defined in section 1.5.3. The Topic Name in the PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT contain wildcard characters [MQTT-3.3.2-2].

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.location: after Topic Name; present when PUBLISH QoS is greater than 0
fields.definition: Identifies a QoS 1 or QoS 2 PUBLISH exchange.
constraints: The value MUST be non-zero when the field is present.

source.excerpt:
The variable header component of many of the Control Packet types includes a 2 byte Packet Identifier field. These Control Packets are PUBLISH (where QoS > 0), PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK.

SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier [MQTT-2.3.1-1].

The variable header contains the following fields in the order: Topic Name, Packet Identifier.

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: The PUBLISH payload contains the Application Message and occupies all bytes after the variable header.

fields.name: Application Message
fields.location: all bytes after the PUBLISH variable header through the end of Remaining Length
fields.representation: zero or more application-defined bytes without an additional MQTT length prefix
fields.definition: Carries the application-specific content being published.
constraints: A zero-length Application Message is valid.
Its byte length is Remaining Length minus the PUBLISH variable-header length.

source.excerpt: The Payload contains the Application Message that is being published. The content and format of the data is application specific. The length of the payload can be calculated by subtracting the length of the variable header from the Remaining Length field that is in the Fixed Header. It is valid for a PUBLISH Packet to contain a zero length payload.

field_overrides.definition: All PUBACK fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
All PUBREC fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
PUBREL fixed-header flags use the reserved value 0010.
All PUBCOMP fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
SUBSCRIBE fixed-header flags use the reserved value 0010.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The SUBSCRIBE variable header contains a Packet Identifier.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.location: SUBSCRIBE variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the SUBSCRIBE request and its corresponding SUBACK.
constraints: The value MUST be non-zero.

source.excerpt:
The variable header component of many of the Control Packet types includes a 2 byte Packet Identifier field. These Control Packets are PUBLISH (where QoS > 0), PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK.

SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier [MQTT-2.3.1-1].

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: The SUBSCRIBE payload contains one or more contiguous Topic Filter and Requested QoS pairs.

fields.name: Topic Filter / Requested QoS pair
fields.location: SUBSCRIBE payload, pairs packed contiguously
fields.definition: Each Topic Filter is immediately followed by its Requested QoS byte.
constraints: A SUBSCRIBE payload MUST contain at least one pair.

source.excerpt:
The payload of a SUBSCRIBE Packet contains a list of Topic Filters indicating the Topics to which the Client wants to subscribe. The Topic Filters in a SUBSCRIBE packet payload MUST be UTF-8 encoded strings as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.8.3-1]. Each filter is followed by a byte called the Requested QoS. This gives the maximum QoS level at which the Server can send Application Messages to the Client.

The payload of a SUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter / QoS pair. A SUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation [MQTT-3.8.3-3].

The upper 6 bits of the Requested QoS byte are not used in the current version of the protocol. They are reserved for future use. The Server MUST treat a SUBSCRIBE packet as malformed and close the Network Connection if any of Reserved bits in the payload are non-zero, or QoS is not 0,1 or 2 [MQTT-3-8.3-4].

members.name: Topic Filter
members.definition: Identifies the set of Topics requested by the Subscription.

members.name: Requested QoS
members.definition: Specifies the maximum QoS level at which the Server can send matching Application Messages.
constraints: The upper six reserved bits MUST be zero.
The Requested QoS value MUST be 0, 1, or 2.

types.name: SUBACK
types.definition: Subscribe acknowledgment containing the acknowledged Packet Identifier and one return code per requested Topic Filter.

field_overrides.definition: All SUBACK fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The SUBACK variable header contains the Packet Identifier from the acknowledged SUBSCRIBE.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.location: SUBACK variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the SUBSCRIBE Packet being acknowledged.
constraints: The value equals the Packet Identifier of the acknowledged SUBSCRIBE.

source.excerpt: The variable header contains the Packet Identifier from the SUBSCRIBE Packet that is being acknowledged.

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: The SUBACK payload contains an ordered list of one-byte return codes.

fields.name: Return Code
fields.location: SUBACK payload, packed contiguously in the order of Topic Filters in the acknowledged SUBSCRIBE
fields.definition: Reports the granted maximum QoS or failure for the corresponding Topic Filter.
constraints: The only allowed values are 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, and 0x80.
There is exactly one Return Code for each Topic Filter in the acknowledged SUBSCRIBE.
Return Code order MUST match Topic Filter order.

source.excerpt: The payload contains a list of return codes. Each return code corresponds to a Topic Filter in the SUBSCRIBE Packet being acknowledged. The order of return codes in the SUBACK Packet MUST match the order of Topic Filters in the SUBSCRIBE Packet. Allowed return codes: 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x80. SUBACK return codes other than 0x00, 0x01, 0x02 and 0x80 are reserved and MUST NOT be used.

types.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
types.definition: Unsubscribe request containing a Packet Identifier and one or more Topic Filters.

field_overrides.definition: UNSUBSCRIBE fixed-header flags use the reserved value 0010.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The UNSUBSCRIBE variable header contains a Packet Identifier.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.location: UNSUBSCRIBE variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the UNSUBSCRIBE request and corresponding UNSUBACK.
constraints: The value MUST be non-zero.

source.excerpt: The variable header contains a Packet Identifier. Section 2.3.1 provides more information about Packet Identifiers.

layout.name: Payload
layout.definition: The UNSUBSCRIBE payload contains one or more MQTT UTF-8 encoded Topic Filters packed contiguously.

fields.name: Topic Filter
fields.location: UNSUBSCRIBE payload, packed contiguously
fields.definition: Identifies a Subscription to remove by exact Topic Filter value.
constraints: The payload MUST contain at least one Topic Filter.
Each Topic Filter MUST be at least one character long.

source.excerpt: The payload for the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet contains the list of Topic Filters that the Client wishes to unsubscribe from. The Topic Filters in an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST be UTF-8 encoded strings as defined in Section 1.5.3, packed contiguously. The Payload of an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter.

types.name: UNSUBACK
types.definition: Unsubscribe acknowledgment with a two-byte variable header and no payload.

field_overrides.definition: All UNSUBACK fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.

source.excerpt: Remaining Length field: This is the length of the variable header. For the UNSUBACK Packet this has the value 2.

layout.name: Variable header
layout.definition: The UNSUBACK variable header contains the Packet Identifier from the acknowledged UNSUBSCRIBE.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.location: UNSUBACK variable header
fields.definition: Identifies the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet being acknowledged.
constraints: The value equals the Packet Identifier of the acknowledged UNSUBSCRIBE.

source.excerpt: The variable header contains the Packet Identifier of the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet that is being acknowledged.

types.name: PINGREQ
types.definition: PING request consisting only of a fixed header with Remaining Length 0; it has no variable header or payload.

field_overrides.definition: All PINGREQ fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
PINGREQ Remaining Length is exactly 0; the packet has no variable header or payload.

source.excerpt: PINGREQ Remaining Length is 0. The PINGREQ Packet has no variable header. The PINGREQ Packet has no payload.

types.name: PINGRESP
types.definition: PING response consisting only of a fixed header with Remaining Length 0; it has no variable header or payload.

field_overrides.definition: All PINGRESP fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
PINGRESP Remaining Length is exactly 0; the packet has no variable header or payload.

source.excerpt: PINGRESP Remaining Length is 0. The PINGRESP Packet has no variable header. The PINGRESP Packet has no payload.

types.name: DISCONNECT
types.definition: Client disconnect notification consisting only of a fixed header with Remaining Length 0; it has no variable header or payload.

field_overrides.definition: All DISCONNECT fixed-header flag bits are reserved and set to zero.
DISCONNECT Remaining Length is exactly 0; the packet has no variable header or payload.

source.excerpt: DISCONNECT Remaining Length is 0. The DISCONNECT Packet has no variable header. The DISCONNECT Packet has no payload.

types.name: Reserved
types.definition: Reserved Control Packet type value; use is forbidden.
